title: Microsubscription prototype scratchpad
body:
Purpose: quick brain-dump for a tiny monthly subscription that targets low-volume interactive apps (chatbots, assistants, internal tools). Want something lower-friction than PAYG for hobbyists and early seats, but cheaper than full committed reserved capacity.

Design constraints / goals:
- keep entry price <$10/mo (psych anchor)
- simple metaphors: "microcredits" map to ~100 tokens of capacity but with session bundling so UX feels natural (not per-token).
- protect SLOs: burst allowed but throttled once a monthly spend threshold reached.
- unit econ needs to be positive for long tail (support + infra), but we accept early losses for acquisition on free-tier-like band.

Key primitives (sketch):
1) Base plan: $6/mo -> includes 50 microcredits (MC).
2) MC: conceptual unit. We define 1 MC ~= 100 tokens of model output (approx). So base gives ~5k tokens output (rough).
3) Session wrapper: opening a conversation consumes 1 MC start (covers prompt + first reply overhead). Subsequent turns consumed against MC at smaller rate: e.g., 1 turn ~= 0.25 MC (gives sticky UX).
4) Overage: additional MC packs sold as $3 for 30 MC (bulk discount).
5) Burst protection: allow temp bursts that convert to conditional throttles if average per-minute rate > threshold.

Rough cost math (back of envelope):
- GPU/token cost (amortized at scale): $0.0000025/token (assume optimized runtime + batching) -> per MC (100 tokens) = $0.00025
- infra overhead (network, storage, orchestration, KVS, logs): add $0.00015/MC
- support + sales + card fees + churn buffer: target $0.001/MC allocated for low-tier
=> marginal cost per MC ~= $0.0014 (conservative)

Revenue math (base plan):
- $6 / month for 50 MC => revenue per MC = $0.12
- gross margin per MC = $0.12 - $0.0014 ~ $0.1186 (very healthy) -> sounds too optimistic vs reality (we likely undercost).

Reality check: common failure modes that blow up cost:
- Short-lived sessions with large system prompts -> 1 session start might be 3k tokens -> 30 MC consumed instantly. Need soft caps or dynamic start-cost.
- Small number of power users consume tons (long-tail). We need friction: rate limits, per-session caps, or incremental pricing tiers.
- If model choice defaults to a heavier variant (e.g., 13B quantized vs small 7B) margins change 2-5x. Need to bind model-class to plan.

Variants to control risk:
A) Model binding: Micro plan limited to small models (gpt-small-like / 7B quantized). Promos to try better models but with explicit surcharge.
B) Session caps: cap session length to 2k tokens by default, with an opt-in plus cost.
C) Decaying free-start: first 3 sessions each month have cheaper start-cost (promo), then normal.
D) Hybrid: $3/mo + included 20 MC, payg per-MC cheaper than retail packs -> lower anchor, encourages commitment.

Behavioral UX notes (to prototype):
- represent MC in conversation header as a progress bar ("you have 16 MC left this month").
- Show estimated MC cost before sending a prompt (like "this message ~2 MC"). Optional, but reduces surprise and support tickets.
- If user hits cheap cap, nudges to upgrade with example use-cases (e.g., "upgrade for long sessions and faster responses").

Example scenarios (concrete):
1) Casual user: 60 short queries/mo, avg 60 tokens/out -> ~36 MC -> stays inside $6 plan.
2) Power hobbyist: 3 long sessions (2k tokens each) + 50 small queries -> 3*(20 MC) + 5 MC = 65 MC -> hits overage -> buys extra pack or upgrades.

Sensitivity table (quick):
- If actual GPU/token is 2x estimated -> marginal cost MC = $0.0029 -> margin still positive but shrinks.
- If users migrate to 13B by default (cost x4) -> break-even evaporates quickly. => must enforce model-class or make differential pricing obvious.

Open questions / TODOs:
- exact mapping token->MC: pick 75/100/150? Leaning to 100 for cognitive simplicity but may bias usage.
- what is the friction threshold that reduces conversion vs acceptance? Need small pilot (A/B): show MC balance vs hidden.
- legal / TOS: do we need explicit policy for session data retention for low-tier? (tie into private deployments nuance) -> loop in Legal.
- implement telemetry to capture session-start token distribution (histogram) for first 10k users before scaling.

Experiment plan (MVP):
- Launch a 2-week pilot via community beta: 500 users, $6/mo (waive for first month?) with telemetry hook. Track 1) avg MC consumption/user, 2) 95th percentile session length, 3) number of users hitting cap.
- A/B: show MC meter vs no meter; measure retention and support tickets.

Notes-to-self: collect historical token histograms from hosted-api for small apps (GH:app-demos) and compute 10th/50th/90th percentiles; adjust MC size.

Links to check (scratch):
- convo-sessionization doc (GH:infra/sessionizer) -> need to coordinate start-cost logic.
- prior mini-tier experiments (JIRA PRIC-12) had conversion ~3.2% for $5 anchor; check cohort-level churn.

Final thought: psychologically, "microsubscription" needs to feel unlimited enough for casual users but bounded for cost control. MC abstraction decouples tokens from users, but visible indicators & gentle caps will reduce abuse while keeping UX friendly.

Random TODOs (short):
- [ ] pick MC->token mapping and lock for pilot
- [ ] decide default model family for micro plan
- [ ] implement telemetry event: microcredit_consumed, session_start_cost, session_end_tokens
- [ ] draft landing copy for UX: emphasize "Simple monthly plan for casual building"

End of scratchpad. Keep this as a personal note; will extract to a one-pager if pilot looks promising.
